goals.name: Mover Training App — Company-Wide Rollout + Driver-Training Port + Digital Training Handbook
goals.assessment: Still Red — a full week of the daily manager push in and engagement has barely moved. Company is at 16% on track: 44 movers on track, 45 at risk, 181 behind, 9 not started or locked (~279 enrolled). That is up only marginally from 42 on track last week, and 181 behind one month from enrollment is the number that matters against the Green gate of 70% through the pipeline by 10/19. The mechanics are right — per-mover velocity view, daily huddle itinerary, weekly-1 manager cadence, QA on sign-offs — but managers are not working their behind lists hard enough for it to show, and it is weak across the board rather than one bad branch. Per-branch on-track / at-risk / behind: Garland 4/1/6 (best ratio), Fort Worth 2/5/9, Tampa 1/3/5, Houston 8/5/18, Dallas 9/7/17, San Antonio 5/4/17, Leander 2/3/16, McKinney 1/5/16, South Austin 5/4/29, North Austin 7/8/40 (worst). The Austins are the deep holes. Honest call is Red until the behind column starts shrinking week over week; 16% one month in does not support a Green read on the last gate.
blockers: Adoption stalled at 16% on track (181 of ~279 behind) — managers not working their behind lists hard enough; weak across all branches, North/South Austin worst

goals.name: Dept-Head/Regional Split — FDE Boots-on-Ground Weeks + Dept-Head QGs as Critical Number
goals.assessment: On track to Super Green — one field week banked, second underway. North Dallas (Aug 25-28) is done: observe-first, then had the team generate their own fixes on OT, damages, and schedule management so ownership sits with the branch. The one open loop from ND is still open — the key issue + action plan is not yet written into the Road-to-A+ HQ. Mike flies to Tampa today, on-site through Thursday for visit #2 of 5. Tampa focus: get ahead of the same OT and schedule-adherence problems Dallas had (Tampa also runs OT), and watch how Steven and Shane manage — sales specifically, since it is Tampa's one red area. Green is 3 field weeks across the 10 branches by Oct 1; Mike is managing to the Super Green 5, plan built and committed. Only risk is competing non-goal workload pulling him out of the field.
blockers: North Dallas key issue + action plan still not written into the Road-to-A+ HQ
Non-goal workload is the standing risk to staying in the field all 5 weeks

goals.name: Fleet Safety Pt 3 — Carry the Red, Restructured
goals.assessment: Green holding, with the accident run as the live watch. Company QTD Samsara is 92 and last week came in at 91; this week's review is still open. The warning-chase backlog stayed clear. The real question is incident rate: six new truck accidents in roughly two weeks are pending review and will likely pull the score once graded — scores are holding on discipline while accident frequency runs hot, which is the tension to watch. Green (>=90 by Oct 1) is comfortably held; Super Green (>=95) is a stretch given the soft middle (Dallas/Garland/McKinney mid-80s) plus the accident overhang. Green for now; re-read once this week's review and the accident grading land.
blockers: Six new truck accidents in ~2 weeks pending review — likely to pull the score once graded (incident rate running hot even as scores hold)

goals.name: Sell Remaining Trucks + Fund 2026 Fleet Purchases
goals.assessment: Moved to Green — the sales engine is running. NWT sold (first truck closed), and the refreshed Marketplace postings pulled real demand: 8 interested buyers on the remaining 4 trucks, most scheduling to see them this week. Green is 3 trucks and Super Green is 5; with 1 already sold and 8 buyers actively looking at 4 units, the trajectory to Green is strong and Super Green (all 5) is genuinely in reach this quarter. Oct 31 is the only clock — no buyer-side deadline pressure. Funds the 2026 fleet purchases.

Green is 1-2 core-process SOPs built and deployed (was 5-6), SG is 3-4 (was 7-8), Samsara Management first, each with a quiz and wiki-ready context. No movement this week, but Mike plans to work on Module 1 this week while in Tampa shadowing. Cameron blessed the shared-build path: if SOP #1 goes clean, Gerald drafts #2-5 and Mike distributes review, ~2 hours per SOP, the lab slot being the real constraint. Yellow — the target is realistic and one deployed module clears Green; the only gap is starting Module 1 in an open slot between field weeks.

weekly_win.win: Worked with Dallas to build out and test a new damage-accountability approach with zero grey area: a clear, objective standard where low performers get coached up or coached out fast. The aim is real, near-term impact on Dallas's damage numbers, which have been the worst in the region — no more slow-rolling C-level damage.
